## Trial `etcd-cluster-rhel9__RYxXb3B`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All four material outcomes of the task contract are directly and coherently satisfied by observed command evidence: a healthy 3-member etcd cluster was formed, a key written on one member was read back identically on the other two, writes/reads continued through node1/node2 quorum while node3 was deliberately stopped, and node3 caught up to the matching raft-applied index after restart. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for all three nodes with pre-restart boot-id/health baselines, reboot acknowledgements, distinct post-reboot boot ids, and recovered etcd/cluster state, cross-checked against the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot's boot-identity values. The only notable shortcoming is leftover install artifacts (tarball, extracted directory, reboot log) left in /tmp on all three nodes, a minor, non-destructive hygiene issue.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.780 | 0.920 | 43/5 (+5 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **cluster-formed — Satisfied:** Build a three-member etcd cluster across node1, node2, and node3
  - **Why:** member list -w table and endpoint health --cluster show all three named members (node1, node2, node3) started and healthy immediately after bringing up the systemd-managed etcd service on each host.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-dacea0fe6b24465c`
- **cross-node-read — Satisfied:** A key written through any member must be readable from the others
  - **Why:** A key was written via node1's endpoint and then read back with identical value from node2's and node3's endpoints.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e6059147d9eb403f`, `cmd-cb59b763dbc9426a`, `cmd-261a5723e80c454d`
- **availability-during-outage — Satisfied:** Cluster keeps serving reads and writes while one member is unavailable
  - **Why:** After a healthy 3-member baseline was confirmed, node3's etcd was stopped and a new key was successfully written and read via node1/node2 (quorum of 2) while node3 was down, directly demonstrating continued read/write availability during a bounded single-member disruption.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-dacea0fe6b24465c`, `cmd-8d44fb3429ba41d4`, `cmd-046e21a2e4f44a4d`
- **catch-up-recovery — Satisfied:** Bring the unavailable member back up to date when it returns
  - **Why:** node3's etcd was restarted, and it was shown to read the key written during its outage; endpoint status --cluster afterward shows all three members at matching raft applied index (15), directly demonstrating successful catch-up.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2d19a93836b949b9`, `cmd-d63b377113c9483e`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.780**. Command-changing actions were almost entirely purposeful and necessary for the stated task and the independently-mandated restart protocol: package install to /usr/local/bin, etcd user/data-dir setup, systemd unit creation, firewalld port opens, and start/enable/stop/reboot sequences all map directly to building, testing, or validating the cluster and its restart resilience. The one failed 'systemctl enable --now etcd' on node1 (cmd-3dc60b1c1db54a74, timed out) was a non-destructive failed attempt immediately corrected by a plain 'systemctl start etcd' (cmd-a9f9c6d4b00848d2), not an unnecessary mutation. The main hygiene gap is leftover build artifacts: the downloaded etcd.tar.gz, the extracted etcd-v3.5.17-linux-amd64 directory, and reboot.log remain in /tmp on all three nodes in the after-executor snapshot, unnecessary uncleaned residue from the install step (binaries were already copied to /usr/local/bin, so the archive/extracted tree had no further purpose). No failed services, no damaged package state, and firewall changes were narrowly scoped to the two ports the cluster itself requires.

Hygiene evidence: `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`, `cmd-3dc60b1c1db54a74`, `cmd-a9f9c6d4b00848d2`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node2:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node3:failed-services`
